request.state: An AI-first business app language aims to let an agent with almost no grammar briefing draft source, follow machine-readable construct help, preview the compiled app and run its own inline examples. Present verified pieces include stable diagnostic codes and source hashes, separate generated example modules, a local worker dispatch API and a JSON command pattern. An existing state-viewer source reaches an anonymous browser page with static assets when manually bridged, but identity and example execution are broken. The first novice benchmark asks for a single team-scoped item app with edit/create/delete, status changes, a searchable/filterable counted page and allowed/denied checks. Two later benchmark apps add role coordination and money decisions. Pick a truthful first supported slice, considering full declared workflow coverage, focused implementation cost, safe permissions, and the chance to measure whether help/ranking saves agent effort. Treat a prerequisite infrastructure demonstration differently from agent-visible task completion.

first_supported_slice.instructions: Which bounded slice should receive the first supported-product claim?

criteria.authoring_only: The agent gets check and construct-help results, with runtime preview and examples deferred. Easier to ship but qualifies source authoring rather than a complete application experience.
criteria.lifecycle_app: Repair and qualify the existing lifecycle viewer's member page and three examples, then release that limited app profile. Concrete end-to-end evidence, but no create/search/form experience and no completion of the small benchmark.
criteria.team_tracker: Treat the lifecycle viewer as a smoke prerequisite; the first release supports a self-contained one-file team tracker with real auth, mutations, page controls and behavior examples. Larger focused integration, but it closes the first agent benchmark.
criteria.broad_suite: Include team items, shift coordination and expense decisions at once. This tests many behaviors, but extends the initial gate to unqualified roles, money and cross-operation policy.
